what: IFEval builds the split pattern r'\s?'+spliter+r'\s?\d+\s?' with no re.escape and no line anchoring, sets num_sections = len(split)-1, and passes on num_sections >= required. The unbounded pattern counts inline cross-references ('see Section 3') and in-word substrings ('subSection3') as section boundaries, so too-few-section answers can pass; and because it requires a digit, spelled-out numbers ('Section One') match nothing and a correct answer fails. Under >= this flips verdicts in both directions.

method.corpus: 7 hand-traced cases (spliter 'Section'); verdict = checker >= vs ground truth.
method.corrected_count: count only line-start spliter keyword + a digit OR a spelled-out number word (case-insensitive).
method.exposure: across GPT-4 responses to the section-requiring prompts: how many have an upstream count above the corrected line-start count (an inline or substring match), and in how many the corrected count flips the >= verdict; examples kept for manual review.
